headline: High: Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-instance design can amplify prompt injection and cascading errors when paired with a prompt-leak corpus, while its allowlisted egress creates leakage/compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a explicitly uses a shared bus with shared state across instances, so attacker-controlled content can traverse the pair’s communication path. agent_b is a prompt-leak corpus, which is exactly the kind of content that can be treated as instructions if ingested. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF agent_b content is fed into agent_a via the shared bus or copied into agent_a inputs
IF agent_a parses external text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared-bus bridging between instances for this pair
Add provenance tags to all agent_b-derived text before agent_a sees it
Strip instruction-like markup from agent_b outputs
requires-engineering: enforce a trusted/untrusted content boundary in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches text, conversation state, audio, video, images, and analytics, and has allowlisted network egress; agent_b has no network egress and no declared data classes. The pair can still leak sensitive conversation content if agent_a forwards shared-state material to external services, but the evidence does not show uncontrolled exfiltration by default.
conditions: IF agent_a forwards shared-bus conversation state to any allowlisted third-party API
IF agent_b-derived prompts contain secrets and are copied into agent_a context
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared conversation state before handoff
Restrict agent_a egress to a single vetted backend
Turn off analytics/telemetry for this pair
requires-engineering: add content-class filtering on the shared bus

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances with shared bus state, while agent_b has no declared concurrency model. That creates a plausible write-conflict path on shared mutable state, but not the high-severity same-directory filesystem/git collision described by the rubric. Uncertainty remains because agent_b’s write surfaces are undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared-bus keys
IF the orchestrator lacks locking or last-writer-wins protection
mitigations: Assign disjoint state namespaces per agent
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Add optimistic concurrency checks on shared state
requires-engineering: introduce locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces conversational and multimodal outputs that agent_b-like prompt repositories can be treated as authoritative inputs for downstream prompting. Because agent_b is a prompt-leak corpus, any unverified reuse of its contents can cascade into incorrect or unsafe actions. The pair lacks evidence of a verification step, so the safer higher severity applies.
conditions: IF agent_b content is used as a prompt template or policy source for agent_a
IF downstream automation trusts agent_a outputs without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before acting on agent_a outputs
Mark agent_b content as non-authoritative reference only
Add a verification step that checks claims against a trusted source
requires-engineering: gate downstream actions behind policy validation

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a can process audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and may send them to third-party APIs via allowlisted egress; agent_b is source-available documentation with no declared data handling. The main compliance risk is residency/retention mismatch for user conversation data flowing through agent_a, not a direct violation from agent_b, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in agent_a conversation state
IF any allowlisted backend stores or processes that data outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Route regulated data only to approved backends
Disable retention-heavy telemetry for regulated sessions
Add a data-class policy banner before processing
requires-engineering: document residency and retention for each allowlisted service
